variants.cost: One new objective evaluation at each trial, including rejected trials; initial objective evaluation separately. Gradient evaluation at a new current point, with reuse possible after rejection. Charge B_k construction/access separately from gradient calls. The source reports one matrix-vector product and three vector products plus quadratic-root work for the Cauchy point (p.252). Any alternative model-step solver incurs its own products, factorizations, iterations and model evaluations; no uniform bound on that work is asserted.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Eq.(1.4), printed p.248; Algorithm 2.1, pp.250–251, Eqs.(2.2)–(2.6); Cauchy-point cost p.252
variants.name: Strictly positive regularization subset of Algorithm 2.1
variants.output: Current accepted iterate x_k at termination, or the sequence of accepted/repeated iterates. No averaging, random output or certified second-order condition is specified.
public_inputs: Exact objective and gradient access; a chosen symmetric model-matrix construction and sufficient access to its products
An explicit subproblem policy satisfying Cauchy decrease; choosing the Cauchy point itself is permitted
variants.query_and_update: Define m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^T s+s^T B_k s/2+sigma_k||s||^3/3. Compute s_k^C=-alpha_k^C g_k, where alpha_k^C minimizes m_k(-alpha g_k) for alpha>=0. Choose any s_k with m_k(s_k)<=m_k(s_k^C), including s_k=s_k^C. Query f(x_k+s_k) and form rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)]/[f(x_k)-m_k(s_k)]. Set x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k if rho_k>=eta_1 and x_{k+1}=x_k otherwise. If rho_k>eta_2 choose sigma_{k+1} in (0,sigma_k]; if eta_1<=rho_k<=eta_2 choose it in [sigma_k,gamma_1 sigma_k]; otherwise choose it in [gamma_1 sigma_k,gamma_2 sigma_k]. Increment k.
variants.requirements: f:R^n->R is C^1; Euclidean norm; B_k=B_k^T; sigma_k>0. Execute ratio steps only when g_k!=0. Higher convergence assumptions and rates are outside this record.
variants.state_and_initialization: Initialize k=0, x_0 and sigma_0. Evaluate/cache f(x_0). At each current point obtain g_k=gradient f(x_k) and a finite symmetric B_k; retain reusable values after rejection. No exact-Hessian assumption is imposed.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: The printed very-successful interval is [0,sigma_k]; this record restricts it to (0,sigma_k], preserving positive regularization. Parameter choices inside these intervals and any better-than-Cauchy subproblem policy remain explicit implementation inputs. The source says until convergence and gives no accuracy stopping rule in Algorithm 2.1. For this selected executable subset terminate and return x_k if g_k=0 before forming rho_k; this is an explicit operational completion, not a claim of second-order optimality. Any tolerance/budget stopping rule must be separately specified and carries no rate here.
